A faithful, authentic rendering of the traditional Indonesian ornament: {subject}.
Style: monochrome line ornament only, pure solid black (#000000) strokes on a fully transparent background, no shading, no gradients, no grey, no texture, no text, no border, no frame.
Composition: a corner ornament like a letterhead flourish or document watermark — the motif is anchored in the bottom-right corner and grows from there, filling roughly the bottom-right two thirds and fading out (fewer, sparser elements) toward the top-left, which stays empty.
Accuracy matters more than decoration: keep the motif's real, recognisable shapes, proportions and symmetry as craftspeople make it; do not invent a generic spiral or mix in other cultures' motifs.

subjects.pintu-aceh: Pinto Aceh (Pintu Aceh) from Aceh, Sumatra, as on the famous Pinto Aceh gold filigree brooch: a symmetrical gateway outline with a gently curved, pointed roof-like top and stepped shoulders, built of several concentric parallel frames; the fields between frames are filled with tiny filigree spirals and small round dots like gold granulation, plus small Acehnese floral (bungong) sprigs. Fine, delicate jewellery-like linework. NOT Gothic tracery, NOT Thai temple ornament, no large leafy vines.
subjects.gorga: Gorga, the carved ornament of the Batak Toba people (North Sumatra) on the gable boards of rumah bolon houses: bold ribbon-like strokes of constant width forming tightly packed pairs of interlocking spirals that face each other (like curled fern shoots meeting), compact and dense, combined with a zigzag sawtooth border band (gorga ipon-ipon) of triangular teeth along the edges. Flat graphic bands as if painted in the Batak red-white-black palette. NOT European/Celtic scrollwork, NO acanthus leaves, NO leaves at all.
subjects.pucuk-rebung: Pucuk Rebung (Pucuak Rabuang), the Malay and Minangkabau bamboo-shoot motif from songket textiles and Rumah Gadang carvings: a row of tall isosceles triangles like young bamboo shoots, each filled with nested chevrons and small curling scrolls, arranged as a border band
subjects.megamendung: Batik Megamendung from Cirebon, West Java: stacked rain-cloud forms, each cloud built from 5 to 9 concentric parallel outlines with characteristic pointed, triangular cloud tips and gentle curls
subjects.kawung: Batik Kawung from Yogyakarta, Java: four ellipses (stylised sugar-palm fruit) meeting at a centre point to form a four-petal cross, repeated on a square diagonal grid, with a small dot or cross in each gap
subjects.batang-garing: Batang Garing, the tree-of-life motif of the Dayak Ngaju people of Central Kalimantan: a vertical spear-tip-shaped tree pointing upward, with paired branches curving symmetrically on both sides ending in curled tips, standing on a base with curled roots and a sacred jar (guci), surrounded by Dayak curling scroll ornament
subjects.patra-punggel: Patra Punggel from Bali as carved in paras stone on candi bentar temple gates: each unit is a chunky curl that bends back on itself — a bulbous mango-seed-shaped core (batun poh), a crest of serrated rooster-comb lobes (janggar siap), jackfruit-pulp-like rounded serrations (ampas nangka) and a tight piglet-ear curl (kuping guling) at the tip; units chained into a running scroll. Crisp, deep, chunky carving forms. NOT European acanthus, NOT baroque, NOT Thai kranok.
subjects.pa-barre-allo: Passura' carving of the Toraja people (South Sulawesi) on tongkonan house walls, featuring Pa' Barre Allo: a round sun disc with curved, petal-like rays, set in a rectangular panel; around it Toraja passura' patterns — Pa' Tedong buffalo-horn crescents, Pa' Bulintong round whorls, and curving S-shaped tendrils with rounded hooks — arranged symmetrically in framed panels and bands, like the carved and painted (red, black, white, yellow) wall panels. NOT Greek meander, NOT Aztec, no square key-fret spirals.
subjects.mamuli: The Mamuli motif from Sumba, East Nusa Tenggara, as woven on hinggi ikat cloth: the omega (Ω)-shaped mamuli ear-ornament form — a closed loop opening into two outward-curling feet — repeated in mirrored rows within horizontal ikat bands with stepped geometric edges
subjects.tenun-tanimbar: Tais, the warp-ikat cloth of the Tanimbar Islands (Yamdena, Maluku): narrow vertical warp stripes, each holding small repeated motifs with blurred, slightly feathered stepped edges typical of warp ikat — a stylised orchid (anggrek) flower, crescent moons, small paired flag shapes, and twin arrowheads (tunis) — separated by plain thin stripes. Rendered as a single-colour line/silhouette ornament. NOT cross-stitch, NOT embroidery, NOT Nordic knitting patterns.
subjects.ukiran-asmat: Asmat wood carving from southern Papua as on Asmat shields (jamasj) and canoe prow ornaments: a tall carved panel in relief whose design is made of mirrored, back-to-back hooked curves and loops — the bipane (double-curved shell nose ornament), the praying-mantis (wenet) limbs as angular bent hooks, hornbill-beak curves and flying-fox wing shapes — with open-work cut-outs and carved grooves outlining each form. Organic, bold, symmetrical. NOT Maori koru, NOT tribal tattoo, NOT Celtic.
